summary: A Button that opens a Menu. The "⋯" overflow menu is this with an icon-only Button. Owns open state, positioning, focus, and the ARIA link between the two.
useWhen: a button opens a list of actions — row actions, an overflow "⋯", a "New" button with several kinds of new
a button opens a list of choices applied immediately, such as a sort order
the actions nest one level or more — submenus open only inside a MenuTrigger

useInstead.when: one action is the common case and the menu holds variations of it — Save, and Save as draft
useInstead.why: a menu hides the common action behind a click; a split button keeps it one press away and puts the variations beside it

useInstead.when: the button opens a form, a filter panel or anything that is not a list of rows
useInstead.why: a menu promises arrow keys between rows and nothing else; a field inside it cannot be reached

useInstead.when: the choice is a form field's value
useInstead.why: a form value is a listbox the form can read, not a menu of actions

useInstead.when: there are only two or three actions and room to show them
useInstead.why: hiding actions behind a menu costs a click and makes them undiscoverable; show them when they fit

composition.note: Exactly two children, in this order: the Button, then the Menu. The Menu is named by the Button unless it has its own aria-label. A MenuItem with a `title` and MenuItem children opens a submenu; `onAction` on the root Menu receives actions from every level.
composition.example: <MenuTrigger><Button variant="tertiary" aria-label="Actions for Payroll" startIcon={<Icon as={Ellipsis} />} /><Menu onAction={(key) => run(key)}><MenuItem key="rename">Rename</MenuItem><MenuItem key="move" title="Move to"><MenuItem key="archive">Archive</MenuItem><MenuItem key="trash">Trash</MenuItem></MenuItem></Menu></MenuTrigger>

bottom start.use: the default — below, aligned to the trigger's start edge

bottom end.use: a trigger at the end of a row or toolbar, so the menu does not run off the edge

top start.use: a trigger near the bottom of the viewport, such as a footer

top end.use: as top start, for a trigger at the end of its row

children.note: the Button first, the Menu second

a11y.role: none — the Button gets aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded; the Menu is the menu
guarantees: Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the menu with focus on its first row; ArrowUp opens it on the last
choosing an action closes every open level and returns focus to the trigger; so do Escape and an outside click
the menu is named by the trigger unless it has its own aria-label
a submenu opens with the right arrow, Enter or Space and closes with the left arrow or Escape, which puts focus back on the row that opened it
submenus are non-modal: the parent menu stays on screen and hoverable, so the pointer can move between levels
requires: an icon-only trigger Button needs its own aria-label — it names the menu too

antiPatterns.dont: wrapping a Menu in a Popover to make a dropdown
antiPatterns.why: the trigger then announces a dialog, not a menu, the arrow keys cannot open it, and choosing an action does not close it. That is exactly what MenuTrigger exists to replace
the trigger must accept react-aria press props and a ref; IonBase's Button does, a DOM button silently never opens

antiPatterns.dont: more than two levels of submenu
antiPatterns.why: each level is a hover target narrower than the last; past two, the pointer falls off the path and the menu closes. Flatten with sections instead
